name: Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (MER-B)
short_description: Opportunity (MER-B) touched down in Meridiani Planum on January 25, 2004 UTC, operating for nearly 15 years (5,111 sols) and driving 28.06 miles (45.16 km)—the off-world driving record. It discovered hematite 'blueberries' and gypsum veins, proving ancient standing liquid water on Mars.

meet_the_explorer.title: Meet the Explorer
meet_the_explorer.introduction: Opportunity (MER-B) was the second of NASA's twin Mars Exploration Rovers, touching down in the smooth equatorial plains of Meridiani Planum on January 25, 2004 UTC (January 24 PST). Designed for a 90-sol (three-month) mission and 1,000 meters of driving, Opportunity achieved one of the most astonishing operational feats in space exploration history: it functioned on Mars for nearly 15 years (5,111 sols), drove a record-setting 28.06 miles (45.16 km)—exceeding an Olympic marathon distance on another world—and discovered conclusive sedimentary evidence that ancient Mars was once soaked in liquid water.

sub_components_represented.name: Opportunity Six-Wheeled Geologic Rover
sub_components_represented.role: Solar-powered mobile field geologist with rocker-bogie mobility and Athena science arm
sub_components_represented.status_at_site: Resting in Perseverance Valley, Endeavour Crater (inactive since June 10, 2018)

sub_components_represented.name: Challenger Memorial Station Lander Platform & Airbags
sub_components_represented.role: Airbag deceleration system and triangular lander petals
sub_components_represented.status_at_site: Resting inside Eagle Crater, Meridiani Planum

mission_and_purpose.title: Mission & Purpose

destination.targeted_feature: Orbital crystalline gray hematite spectral signature

landing_or_orbital_coordinates.coordinate_standard: IAU Planetocentric Standard (Challenger Memorial Station, Eagle Crater)

coordinate_discrepancies.notes: Touchdown occurred at 21:05 PST on Jan 24, corresponding to 04:54 UTC on Jan 25.

objectives: Investigate Meridiani Planum, targeted because orbital spectrometers had detected widespread crystalline gray hematite, a mineral typically formed in water.
Search for and analyze stratified rock outcrops, sedimentary structures, and mineral veins left by ancient bodies of standing or groundwater.
Determine whether the local environmental conditions were acidic, saline, or neutral, and evaluate their past habitability for microbial life.
Perform ground truth calibration for Mars orbiters (MGS, Odyssey, MRO).
Study impact crater morphology across dozens of craters ranging in size from small pits to the 14-mile-wide Endeavour Crater.

meet_the_technology.title: Meet the Technology
meet_the_technology.architecture_description: Six-wheeled robotic rover with rocker-bogie mobility chassis, carrying a mast-mounted stereo color imaging suite and a 5-degree-of-freedom robotic arm. Modified in flight to operate purely in volatile RAM mode following flash memory sector wear.

mass_discrepancies.resolution_or_erratum: Both spacecraft had an identical canonical metric mass of 185.0 kg; imperial conversions represent slight table rounding differences (407.9 lb).

propulsion.type: Six-Wheel Independent Electric Drive with Front and Rear Steering
propulsion.engines_or_thrusters: Six brushed DC drive motors in wheel hubs; capable of driving slopes up to 32 degrees
propulsion.thrust_rating: Not applicable (surface mobile rover driven by six brushed DC electric wheel-hub motors with torque of up to 40 N·m per wheel)

power_system.primary_power_source: Gallium Arsenide Solar Array with Rechargeable Lithium-Ion Batteries
power_system.solar_array_details: Multi-junction solar array providing ~700 to 900 Wh/sol under clear conditions, dropping below 22 Wh/sol during the June 2018 global dust storm.

nuclear_rtg_details.power_decay_profile: Eight 1-Watt thermal pellets positioned inside central electronics bay to protect electronics against -100°C temperatures.

frequency_bands: UHF (relay through MGS, Odyssey, and MRO)
communications.relay_systems: UHF relay via orbiters provided over 90% of all downlinked science data and imagery.

scientific_instruments.name: Panoramic Camera
scientific_instruments.purpose: Multispectral, stereoscopic, high-resolution color imaging of Mars topography and minerals.
scientific_instruments.specifications: Mast-mounted stereo cameras with 16-position filter wheels.

scientific_instruments.name: Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer
scientific_instruments.purpose: Identify minerals, carbonates, silicates, and clays from thermal infrared spectra at long distances.

scientific_instruments.name: Microscopic Imager
scientific_instruments.purpose: Examine fine-scale geological textures, spherical concretions ('blueberries'), and mineral veins.

scientific_instruments.name: Mössbauer Spectrometer
scientific_instruments.purpose: Determine iron oxidation states and identify minerals like jarosite and hematite.
scientific_instruments.specifications: Arm-mounted backscatter spectrometer with cobalt-57 source.
scientific_instruments.operational_status: Operated until isotope source decay in later mission.

scientific_instruments.name: Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer
scientific_instruments.purpose: Quantify elemental rock chemistry and abundances of major elements.
scientific_instruments.specifications: Arm-mounted curium-244 alpha and X-ray source.

scientific_instruments.name: Rock Abrasion Tool
scientific_instruments.purpose: Grind through rock rinds to expose unweathered interiors.
scientific_instruments.specifications: Diamond-tipped grinding wheel; aluminum cuff manufactured from World Trade Center recovery metal.

the_journey.title: The Journey
the_journey.journey_narrative: Opportunity launched on July 7, 2003, and landed on January 25, 2004 UTC, scoring an interplanetary 'hole in one' by rolling to a halt directly inside 22-meter Eagle Crater. Over the next 15 years, it embarked on an epic overland campaign across Meridiani Planum, exploring Endurance, Victoria, and Endeavour craters. It overcame sand entrapment in Purgatory Dune, passed the Olympic marathon driving distance in March 2015, and continued science until June 10, 2018, when a catastrophic global dust storm cut off solar power in Perseverance Valley.

arrival_event.touchdown_velocity_or_approach_speed: Touchdown impact speed 14 m/s (bounced 26 times inside airbags)
arrival_event.arrival_notes: Interplanetary 'hole in one' landing directly inside Eagle Crater.

mission_timeline.event_description: Rolled to a stop inside Eagle Crater; immediate imaging revealed exposed bedrock and hematite blueberries.
Drove into 130-meter-wide Endurance Crater, conducting systematic stratigraphy of ancient sedimentary rock layers.
Became bogged down in soft sand ripple for six weeks; successfully extricated on June 4 after extensive laboratory simulation.
Traversed to and explored Victoria Crater (800 m wide), analyzing cliff walls at Duck Bay.
Passed the official Olympic marathon distance (26.219 miles / 42.195 km) on Sol 3,968.

mission_timeline.phase: Catastrophic Global Dust Storm & Final Contact
mission_timeline.event_description: Planet-encircling dust storm dropped solar array power from 650 Wh/sol to <22 Wh/sol. Opportunity sent its final transmission on June 10, 2018. Mission officially concluded Feb 13, 2019.

scientific_discoveries.title: Scientific Discoveries
scientific_discoveries.summary_narrative: Opportunity transformed planetary geology by discovering conclusive sedimentary evidence of standing bodies of liquid water, cross-bedded sandstones, gypsum veins, and neutral-pH clay epochs on Mars.

key_discoveries.title: Hematite 'Blueberries' & Acidic Groundwater Sediments
key_discoveries.description: Discovered millions of millimeter-scale spherical hematite concretions ('blueberries') weathering out of sulfate-rich sandstones at Eagle and Fram craters, proving water-saturated sediments.
key_discoveries.scientific_impact: Proved conclusively that acidic, saline liquid water once soaked the plains of Meridiani Planum.

key_discoveries.title: Jarosite & Evaporite Mineral Beds
key_discoveries.description: Detected jarosite (a hydrous potassium-iron sulfate mineral) in stratified bedrock, establishing that rocks formed in shallow evaporating surface waters.
key_discoveries.scientific_impact: First direct in-situ confirmation of evaporite sedimentary rocks on another planet.

key_discoveries.title: Homestake Gypsum Mineral Vein
key_discoveries.description: Discovered a bright mineral fracture vein named 'Homestake' on Endeavour's rim, confirmed to be pure calcium sulfate (gypsum).
key_discoveries.scientific_impact: Provided unequivocal evidence of water flowing through underground rock fractures in a non-acidic, milder chemical environment.

key_discoveries.title: Ancient Neutral-pH Smectite Clays at Pillinger Point
key_discoveries.description: Discovered smectite clay minerals formed in neutral-pH, fresh water on the rim of Endeavour Crater.
key_discoveries.scientific_impact: Proved that early Mars had a benign, neutral-water era that was significantly more hospitable to microbial life than the younger acidic epoch.

where_is_it_now.title: Where Is It Now?
where_is_it_now.location_summary: Rests on the upper slope of Perseverance Valley on the western rim of Endeavour Crater, Meridiani Planum, Mars (1.9483° S, 354.47417° E).
where_is_it_now.why_left_behind: Designed as an in-situ robotic surface rover with no ascent or return capability. Succumbed to power exhaustion during the planetary dust storm of June 2018.

hardware_elements_at_site.condition: Resting intact on the rocky slope of Perseverance Valley, facing eastward
Resting 45.16 km away at the touchdown site inside Eagle Crater

its_legacy.title: Its Legacy
its_legacy.historical_significance: Opportunity holds the all-time off-world distance driving record (28.06 miles / 45.16 km), demonstrating that robotic field geologists can operate for over a decade in extreme alien environments and proving that Mars was once a water-soaked world.
key_contributions: Held the off-world distance driving record for any vehicle in human history.
Proved that liquid water was once persistent and widespread on the surface of Mars.
Established the operational methodologies, autonomous drive protocols, and flash memory recovery procedures used by modern Mars missions.
Operated across 5,111 sols (over 55 times its 90-sol design lifespan).

influence_on_future_missions.influence_description: Overland navigation software, long-distance route selection, and rover energy management standards developed during Opportunity's 15-year drive directly shaped MSL and Mars 2020 operations.

its_legacy.cultural_or_philosophical_impact: Affectionately known as 'Oppy', the rover captivated the global public for a generation; its final message before the dust storm ('My battery is low and it's getting dark') became a poetic touchstone of space exploration.
